decisions.title: Agent branches and review model
decisions.decision: Every agent pushes only to agent/<their-id> and opens a pull request into main. The founder reviews and merges. Agents never merge, never push to main, never force-push.
decisions.reasoning: A single unreviewed writer is how a working codebase becomes a broken one. A branch plus a PR gives every change a review surface and a clean revert point.
rejected_alternatives: Agents committing directly to main — no review surface, no revert point
Automated merging on green CI — CI does not check product judgement

decisions.title: Agents communicate through committed JSON, not prose
decisions.decision: Coordination lives in agents/state/{tasks,handoffs,blockers,decisions}.json, committed to the repository. Every agent reads all four at session start. Append-only history.
decisions.reasoning: Prose handoffs are paraphrased or forgotten between sessions. A structured record with ids, owners, timestamps and evidence survives a session ending and a different agent picking the work up.
rejected_alternatives: Free-text notes in conversation/ — not committed, so a fresh clone has no context
GitHub Issues only — not visible to an agent reading the repo; duplicates state

decisions.title: No package installation without founder approval
decisions.decision: No agent installs any package, library, or dependency without explicit founder approval, sought through a blockers entry.
decisions.reasoning: Every dependency is a supply-chain and maintenance liability. This project has already shipped two leaked-credential incidents and an abandoned second stack; dependency drift is the same class of uncontrolled change.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing dev dependencies freely — dev deps still run in CI and on the founder's machine

decisions.title: Verify by running, and prove the test can fail
decisions.decision: Before reporting any check as passing, revert the fix and show the check failing. Every handoff must include the commands run and their results.
decisions.reasoning: This rule has caught six real defects on this project, including two security properties and a test that was passing over an empty list. A check that cannot fail manufactures confidence, which is worse than no check.
rejected_alternatives: Trusting a green suite — green is not evidence that the test exercised the behaviour

decisions.title: Stale planning documents: trust the tree
decisions.decision: When a planning document and the repository disagree, the repository wins, and the conflict is recorded in a handoff. Verify a component exists before building it.
decisions.reasoning: Three successive planning documents described the repo months out of date, and following one literally would have deleted working file upload. Six items across two scopes were already built.
rejected_alternatives: Following the document and adjusting during implementation — that is how capability gets deleted
